landing.meta_title: TrustPages — Answer security reviews before they're asked
landing.meta_description: Monitor your vendors' sub-processor pages, keep dated evidence of every change, and publish a public trust page your customers can subscribe to. Free for 3 vendors, permanently — no card.
landing.hero_title: Sub-processor compliance with cryptographic proof — automated.
landing.hero_body: Track vendor privacy policy updates, filter noise with AI, approve real changes, and provide auditors with tamper-proof SHA-256 HTML evidence. Set up in 60 seconds.
landing.hero_note: Free plan is permanent. New accounts get 14 days of the paid plan first.
landing.card1_body: Send one link instead of filling in the same vendor questions on every security review. Buyers see a professional, auditable compliance presence — even if you're a five-person team.
landing.card2_title: Never miss a vendor change — or drown in false ones
landing.card2_body: Unlike a simple page-diff scraper, TrustPages classifies every detected change with Gemini 2.5 Flash. A reworded footer or a moved menu item publishes itself as cosmetic; only a genuine sub-processor change ever reaches your approval queue.
landing.card3_body: Approved changes publish to your trust page and notify your subscribers by email — your notification obligation, handled without a single manual announcement.
landing.notion_title: Why not just a Notion page?
landing.notion_body: A static page can't tell you when Stripe quietly adds a new sub-processor, and it can't email your customers about it. TrustPages is the difference between claiming you track your vendors and being able to prove it — with a live change history your buyers can audit. And it costs a fraction of enterprise compliance platforms you don't need yet.
landing.screenshots_body: A screenshot can be cropped, edited or retaken to say whatever the week of the audit needs it to say — there is no way for anyone but you to check. Every change TrustPages detects instead stores the vendor's raw HTML itself, fingerprinted with an independent SHA-256 hash, a UTC capture timestamp and a unified diff against the previous version — bundled into one downloadable ZIP an auditor can verify without trusting our dashboard at all.
landing.audit_title: What you can hand an auditor
landing.audit_sub: A screenshot taken the week of the audit proves nothing about what the page said three months ago.
landing.audit1_title: The documents, not just the diff
landing.audit1_body: Every detected change stores the vendor's page as it read before and after, each with a content hash and a timestamp — plus who reviewed it and when they approved it.
landing.audit2_title: One CSV for the whole history
landing.audit2_body: Export every change as a single file: dates, vendors, classifications, hashes and decisions — the thing you actually get asked for. Part of the Growth plan.
landing.audit3_body: Your DPA promises customers a heads-up under Article 28(2). We draft that notice from the change itself, so the part that usually gets skipped is a review rather than a blank page.
landing.demo_sub: One dashboard for you, one public trust page for your customers.

landing.demo_cap2: Your public trust page: live status, change history, subscriber notifications.

pricing.why1_t: The objection window is short and it starts without you
pricing.why1_b: Under GDPR Article 28(2), a processor working from a general authorisation has to tell you before it adds or replaces a sub-processor, and you get a window to object — typically 10 to 30 days in a commercial DPA. In practice that notice is a quiet update to a page on their site. If nobody is watching the page, the window closes on its own.
pricing.why2_t: "When did that change?" is a question you have to answer with a date
pricing.why2_b: A screenshot taken the week of the audit proves nothing about what the page said three months ago. Every change here is stored with its diff and its timestamp, from the day you started monitoring.
pricing.why3_t: Your customers ask you the same question you ask your vendors
pricing.why3_b: The trust page turns your answer into something you publish once instead of writing out in every security questionnaire — a public, dated history of your sub-processor changes that customers can subscribe to.
pricing.why4_t: Audit-Ready Proof: the file itself, not a link to our dashboard
pricing.why4_b: Every change can be downloaded as a self-contained ZIP — the vendor's raw HTML before and after, the diff, both content hashes, and your approval and customer-notice trail in one file. Hand it to an auditor or an enterprise customer's security review without asking them to trust that our site still shows the same thing next year.
pricing.faq1_a: Partly, and it's worth being precise about which part. DORA requires EU financial entities to keep a Register of Information covering their ICT providers and those providers' subcontractors, filed with the regulator each year. TrustPages keeps the subcontractor half of that current and dated. It is not a filing tool and it does not produce the register for you.
pricing.faq2_q: How does the AI tell material changes from cosmetic ones?
pricing.faq2_a: Every detected diff is classified as material or cosmetic. Cosmetic changes — typos, reformatting, a moved heading — publish automatically. Anything that could affect your customers, such as a new sub-processor or a new processing country, goes to your approval queue first. You always have the final say before it reaches your trust page.
pricing.faq3_a: Nothing is charged, and the account does not stop working: it settles onto the free plan, where your 3 oldest pages keep being checked daily. Anything above that is switched off rather than deleted, so upgrading later turns it back on with its history intact.
pricing.faq4_q: What if I need to track more than 30 vendors?
pricing.faq4_a: 30 covers the vendor list of most teams at this size. If you need more, email us and we'll sort out a limit increase on the Growth plan.
pricing.faq5_a: Yes, from the billing page in your dashboard. You keep Growth until the end of the period you've already paid for, and then the account continues on the free plan rather than closing — your trust page stays online and your change history stays intact, so cancelling doesn't take down a public page your customers may have bookmarked.
pricing.faq5_link: See our refund policy for the 14-day money-back guarantee on your first paid period.

vendor.why_title: Why this matters if you use {vendor}
vendor.why_body: Under GDPR Article 28(2), your own customers are usually entitled to notice before you add or replace a sub-processor — and {vendor}'s sub-processors are part of that chain. The notice period in a typical DPA is 10 to 30 days, and it starts when the vendor updates their page, not when you notice.

compare.categories.name: Lightweight subprocessor registries
compare.categories.shape: A hosted page listing your sub-processors, refreshed by daily checks of the vendors you name. The closest neighbours to what we do.
compare.categories.price: Free for a handful of vendors, roughly $19-$49/month for more or unlimited
strengths: Cheapest route to unlimited vendors, by a wide margin
Custom subdomain for the public page at the lower paid tiers
Free tiers exist, though they usually carry the vendor's own mark on your page
limits: The record is generally the current state plus alerts, not a dated document per change
Review before publishing is thin or absent — updates tend to flow automatically
Coverage is limited to the vendors the tool already tracks
compare.categories.pick_them_when: You have a long vendor list, a small budget, and nobody is going to ask you to prove what a page said last quarter.

compare.categories.name: Privacy-team evidence suites
compare.categories.shape: Built for a privacy function with several people in it: monitoring plus review queues, evidence capture, and records-of-processing and transfer-assessment modules.
compare.categories.price: Around €99/month entry, €299 for the review workflow, €999 for roles and modules
strengths: Role-based access for privacy, legal and procurement working the same queue
RoPA and Transfer Impact Assessment alongside the monitoring
Stated EU data residency and a DPA available before purchase
limits: The review workflow and audit export sit two tiers up, not in the entry plan
The evidence faces inward, at your auditor — there is no public page for your customers
Trials are short and there is no permanent free plan
compare.categories.pick_them_when: More than one person reviews vendor changes, or you need RoPA and TIA in the same tool. We cannot serve a two-person privacy team; they can.

compare.categories.name: General page-change monitors
compare.categories.shape: Not compliance products. They watch any URL and tell you it moved, with an AI summary and an importance score.
compare.categories.price: Free for a handful of pages, roughly $13-$85/month for hundreds
strengths: Far cheaper per page, and hundreds of pages rather than dozens
Alerts anywhere — Slack, Teams, Discord, webhooks
Element-level selectors and automatic discovery of new pages
limits: The output is a notification, not evidence: no decision trail, no audit export
Nothing to show a customer — no public page, no subscriber notice
Nothing drafts the Article 28(2) message your DPA promises
compare.categories.pick_them_when: You want to know when pages change and you will handle the compliance side yourself, in a spreadsheet you already keep.

compare.categories.name: Trust centre and GRC platforms
compare.categories.shape: The enterprise end: a full trust centre with questionnaire automation, certifications, NDA-gated documents, and sub-processors as one section of many.
compare.categories.price: Typically annual contracts, four to five figures
strengths: Answers the entire security review, not only the sub-processor part
Document libraries, access controls, integrations with the rest of the stack
The name on the page carries weight with an enterprise buyer
limits: Priced and scoped for a company with a compliance function
Sub-processor monitoring is a feature, not the focus, and is often manual
Weeks to deploy rather than an afternoon
compare.categories.pick_them_when: Security questionnaires are a recurring cost across your whole company and you have the budget to solve all of it at once.

compare.position.title: The documents, not just the diff
compare.position.body: Every detected change stores the vendor's page as it read before and after, each with a content hash and a timestamp, plus who reviewed it and when. “What did this page say in March” has an answer.

compare.position.title: Nothing publishes without you
compare.position.body: Changes are classified material or cosmetic, and only high-confidence cosmetic edits publish themselves. Everything else waits in a queue with a side-by-side diff.

compare.position.title: Export on every plan
compare.position.body: The whole history leaves as one CSV — dates, vendors, classifications, hashes, decisions — including on the free plan. It is the file you actually get asked for.

compare.position.title: The customer notice, drafted
compare.position.body: Your DPA promises customers a heads-up under Article 28(2). We draft it from the change itself, so the step that usually gets skipped is a review rather than a blank page.

compare.position.title: Any URL, including the awkward ones
compare.position.body: Pages that only render with JavaScript are fetched with a real browser, so coverage is not limited to a list of vendors we happen to track.

compare.gaps: 30 pages on the top plan, where cheaper tools offer unlimited.
The public trust page lives on a usetrustpages.com address; there is no custom domain yet.
Email alerts only — no Slack, no webhooks, no API.
One login per account: no roles for a privacy team working together.
No RoPA, no Transfer Impact Assessments, no questionnaire automation.
